lemma: Lemma T (cut lemma, arbitrary gate semantics). Let C be a circuit over inputs x=(a,b), a in {0,1}^{n_A}, b in {0,1}^{n_B}, whose gates compute arbitrary Boolean functions of any fan-in. Let S be a set of gates closed under gate-predecessors (each gate input of a gate in S is in S or is an A-variable). Let kappa_E(S) be the number of wires into gates outside S that originate from an A-variable or from a gate in S. Then the number D of distinct rows of M_f[a,b]=f(a,b) satisfies log2 D <= kappa_E(S). Proof: each gate in S depends only on a, so the crossing-wire message m(a) in {0,1}^{kappa_E} is a function of a. Each gate outside S is a function of its in-neighbours (b-variables, A-variables, crossing wires, or outside gates), so by induction over outside gates f(a,b)=G(m(a),b). Row a is determined by m(a), hence D <= 2^{kappa_E}. If the output lies in S, f depends on a only and D=1.
gap: Lemma T does not by itself bound kappa_E(S) for a circuit class with a locality or size restriction; the open point of K9-D1 is whether a bounded-fan-in, size-s circuit admits an S with kappa_E(S) small enough to contradict the rank of M_f. Next: derive kappa_E(S) <= d * (number of gates touching the cut) and test whether a balanced cut of size s exists for the target class.
proved_step: CLAIMED: Lemma T as stated in lemma field. Scope: any gate semantics, any fan-in, finite circuits; the bound uses only that each gate is a function of its in-neighbours. Honest note: this is the standard cut/communication bound restated for arbitrary gates; it is correct but elementary. It transfers the K9-D1 cut argument verbatim; B2-specific edge counts (2 inputs, 16 truth tables) do not enter.

lemma: Lemma T' (repair of S0001, self-correction, not a review). C: circuit over x=(a,b), arbitrary gate functions of any fan-in; S: set of gates closed under gate-predecessors; kappa_E(S): number of wires into gates outside S that come from an A-variable or from a gate in S. Then log2 D <= kappa_E(S) + [output gate in S], where D = number of distinct rows of M_f[a,b]=f(a,b). Proof: if the output gate is outside S, the crossing-wire message m(a) determines f(a,b)=G(m(a),b), so D <= 2^{kappa_E}. If the output gate lies in S, f(a,b)=h(a) and the rows take at most the two values constant 0 and constant 1, so D <= 2 = 2^{kappa_E+1} when kappa_E=0 is possible.
gap: S0001 stated D=1 when the output lies in S; that is false (copy-gate counterexample: D=2, kappa_E=0). The bound log2 D <= kappa_E is refuted in that case; Lemma T' is the corrected form. Lemma T' remains an elementary cut bound and does not by itself close G0001 (bounding kappa_E(S) for a size-s or locality-restricted class). Next: test H1 (S0001 as stated) vs H2 (Lemma T') on random circuits.
refuted_approach: S0001 case 'output in S implies D=1': refuted by one copy gate (f = a_1). Repair: additive +1 in the output-in-S case.

lemma: Lemma T' status: CLAIMED (self-proof plus sampled test cm-8c3ad727be60432a). Not a review. Still needs a review by a session of another model family. G0001 remains open: T' bounds the cut by kappa_E, but for a size-s, bounded-fan-in circuit it is still unknown whether an S with kappa_E(S) small exists for the target class.
evidence: EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION cm-8c3ad727be60432a (DISCOVERY, K9-D1). 4000 random circuits, nA,nB in 1..3, up to 6 gates, fan-in 1..3, arbitrary truth tables; S built so every S-gate reads only A-variables or S-gates (the lemma's hypothesis). Result: output_in_S 340, of which D=2 in 197. H1 (S0001 as stated, log2 D <= kappa_E) violated 78 times; first example: one gate g=a_0 with table [1,0], S={g}, kappa_E=0, D=2. H2 (T': log2 D <= kappa_E + [output in S]) violated 0 times. Earlier run cm-059410913bfb4ca5 had 108 H2 violations; the cause was a harness bug (S-gates could read B-variables, violating the hypothesis), fixed in this run. Prediction matched: H1 fails exactly in the output-in-S case; T' holds on the sample. Scope: sampled finite circuits only; T' itself has a hand proof (output in S => f(a,b)=h(a) => rows are constant, so D<=2; output outside S => D<=2^kappa_E). The test does not close G0001.

gap: Does not give the cut-cost bound kappa_E for balanced cuts (open part of G0001). Refutes nothing. The +1 of Lemma T' is superfluous (the bound 2^T holds). Random and exhaustive experiments cm-86abb056af304e8b and cm-cd2b32fe804d4cbf are consistent with 2^T but do not separate it from 2^(T+1). Model family of the author is shared with the claimers: needs review by a different family before any submit_claim.
proved_step: Cut rank bound with arbitrary gate semantics: for a circuit whose gates each compute an arbitrary function of their input wires (any fan-in), with T = number of wires owned by one side that feed a gate on the other side, rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^T for M_f[a,b]=f(a,b). Proof: order cross wires topologically; the transcript tau in {0,1}^T gives rectangles R_tau = A_tau x B_tau (consistency conditions are per-party); on R_tau the output is a function of the owner's input alone (its owner knows its input and all received transcript bits), so M restricted to R_tau has rank <= 1; sum over 2^T transcripts.
